title: Effects of sleep symptomatology post-concussion on return to sport in collegiate athletes.

sections.label: OBJECTIVE
sections.text: To describe the relationship between sleep-symptom severity and number of days to return to play following concussion in student-athletes.

sections.label: SETTING
sections.text: A D1 NCAA university athletic department (institutional care).

sections.label: PARTICIPANTS
sections.text: The study enrolled 84 varsity athletes who suffered a sport-related concussion at the university from 2015 to 2021.

sections.label: INDEPENDENT VARIABLES
sections.text: Prior concussion(s), total symptom burden, and sleep symptomatology (sleeping more, sleeping less, trouble falling asleep, drowsiness, and fatigue) scores as reported using Post-Concussion Symptom Scale from the Immediate Post-Concussion Assessment and Cognitive Testing (ImPACT).

sections.label: MAIN OUTCOME MEASURE
sections.text: The number of days an athlete took to return to play following concussion.

sections.label: RESULTS
sections.text: Individuals who reported trouble falling asleep, sleeping less, fatigue, and drowsiness took significantly longer to return to play following concussion than individuals who did not report such symptoms (F1,102 = 34.12, p < 0.0001).

sections.label: CONCLUSIONS
sections.text: Sleep symptomatology present after concussion is predictive of days until return to sport. This study demonstrates the importance of sleep symptomatology post-concussion for athletes.
